label: TP
reason: The CodeQL report identifies two distinct vulnerabilities: insecure randomness (using java.util.Random which is cryptographically weak) and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). The insecure randomness is confirmed by the code using new java.util.Random().nextInt() to generate a session key (line 111), which is unsuitable for security-sensitive tokens like rememberMeKeys. The XSS vulnerability is confirmed by the direct concatenation of user-controllable strings from HTTP headers (param derived from request.getHeaderNames() and Cookie values) into HTML responses via PrintWriter.println() (lines 120-125) without any HTML entity encoding.

evidence.note: Uses insecure java.util.Random instead of SecureRandom for generating sensitive session token
Directly writes unencoded user input from request headers and cookies into HTML response
